builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: System 1 agents: a method for local, reliable and fast agentic AI
summary: This method replaces generative LLM-based tool use with a deterministic compiler and a small decision model that selects tools and arguments via multiple-choice classification. It costs significantly less memory and compute than running a local LLM and eliminates hallucinated values in tool calls by design. It can fail when the agent must reason over implicit context, handle novel tool combinations not covered by the compiled options, or manage complex multi-step planning that requires generative flexibility.
rationale: The technique eliminates hallucination in tool calls and operates on constrained hardware by replacing generative inference with classification, matching the reader's production constraints.
technique: Deterministic compiler-based tool selection without text generation

claims.statement: This method replaces generative LLM-based tool use with a deterministic compiler and a small decision model that selects tools and arguments via multiple-choice classification. It costs significantly less memory and compute than running a local LLM and eliminates hallucinated values in tool calls by design. It can fail when the agent must reason over implicit context, handle novel tool combinations not covered by the compiled options, or manage complex multi-step planning that requires generative flexibility.

The System 1 agent chose the right tool, or correctly declined, for 97.0% of requests, significantly ahead of all 18 local LLM-agent settings (best 95.2%). No System 1 call contained invented content, against 5.5-19.7% of LLM calls.
